around.headline: Hebbal short tunnel's traffic relief may only be temporary, IISc study warns
around.summary: A fresh IISc study says the short tunnel at Hebbal could ease congestion only in the near term and may create new choke points, with queues building up inside the tunnel itself, per today's reports. If Hebbal is on your regular route, don't bank on the relief lasting — keep a buffer in your commute time.

around.headline: Traffic diversions in place today for Eid Milad-un-Nabi procession
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police have diversions in place for today's Eid Milad-un-Nabi procession routes, per today's reports. Check for local diversions before heading out if your commute passes through affected stretches today.

around.headline: Parking feuds see Bengaluru neighbours flagging each other's cars as 'abandoned'
around.summary: Residents are increasingly reporting neighbours' long-parked vehicles as 'abandoned' to civic authorities amid ongoing street-parking disputes, per today's report. If street parking is tight where you live, a car left too long in one spot — even your own — could now draw a civic complaint.

around.headline: 8 Bengaluru clubs face action over hygiene lapses, cockroach infestation
around.summary: Food safety inspections at several Bengaluru clubs turned up expired meat and cockroach infestations, with 8 clubs now facing action; Karnataka's health minister said the focus should be on kitchen hygiene, not dress codes, per today's reports. Worth a second thought before your next night out at a club or pub in the city.

around.headline: Study questions whether Bengaluru's diverted sewage still ends up polluting lakes
around.summary: A new study examined what actually happens to Bengaluru's sewage after it's diverted away from lakes, and the findings raise doubts about how effective that diversion has really been, per today's report. Worth knowing if you live near a lake billed as 'cleaned up' — the underlying pollution problem may not be fully solved.

around.headline: US again weighing a $100,000 fee on H-1B visas
around.summary: Reports say the US administration is once again considering a steep $100,000 fee on H-1B visas, a move that would hit Indian IT workers and the companies that sponsor them hardest, per today's report. If you or your employer relies on H-1B sponsorship, it's worth tracking closely before making near-term travel or relocation plans.

street_smart.title: You ride to a crowded Bengaluru market street to grab something quickly — in and out in two minutes. What's the smartest way to park your two-wheeler?
street_smart.based_on: No single incident in today's feeds fits the choice-based trap format cleanly, so this rotates in from the evergreen list: two-wheeler theft prevention. This specific topic hasn't appeared as the street-smart scenario in the last three weeks of briefs (Aug 6–26), which instead covered tenant/rental traps, UPI fraud, auto/cab overcharging, job scams, medical emergencies, loan-app harassment, credit-card skimming, phone snatching, consumer court basics, and several one-off safety incidents.
street_smart.situation: The street is crowded, there's no marked parking bay nearby, and you don't want to lose your spot by hunting for one.

choices.text: Walk a bit further to the nearest paid or marked parking area, and additionally lock the wheel with a portable disc lock before leaving.
choices.feedback: Correct. A disc lock or chain defeats what a bike's built-in steering lock alone can't: many two-wheeler thefts take under a minute once the steering lock is picked or the bike is simply lifted and wheeled away. Paid or marked parking areas also usually have some attendant presence or CCTV, both of which casual thieves specifically avoid.

choices.text: Park right where you are, on the roadside, since you'll only be gone two minutes and the street is busy anyway.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. 'Just two minutes' is exactly the window most two-wheeler thefts happen in — a busy street doesn't protect you, since a bike being wheeled away doesn't look unusual in a crowd, and a steering lock alone can be defeated in seconds with a duplicate key or basic tools.

choices.text: Park in a quiet lane just off the main street, thinking it's safer away from the crowd.
choices.feedback: Risky — a quiet lane with no foot traffic and no CCTV actually gives a thief more time and less chance of being noticed, not less. Crowds aren't inherently protective, but total privacy for a thief is worse.

choices.text: Ask a nearby shopkeeper to keep an eye on it while you run in.
choices.feedback: This helps a little, but a shopkeeper busy with their own customers isn't a substitute for a physical lock — most won't notice until the bike is already gone. Treat it as a backup to a disc lock, not a replacement for one.

takeaways: A steering/handlebar lock alone isn't enough — carry a small disc lock or chain for any stop longer than a minute, especially in crowded spots where a bike being wheeled away won't draw attention.
Keep a photo of your RC and insurance on your phone and know your chassis/engine number — these are the first things police and insurers ask for if you need to file a theft report.
If your bike is stolen, file a police FIR within 24 hours (needed for the insurance claim) and inform your insurer right away — delays beyond the policy's notice window can affect the payout.
